definitions.explanation: The act of avenging a wrong, especially killing someone to avenge the death of a family member or lord. Historically an important concept in samurai culture.

examples.japanese: {忠臣蔵|ちゅうしんぐら}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{仇討|あだう}ちの{物語|ものがたり}だ。
examples.english: Chushingura is a famous story of vengeance.

examples.japanese: {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}には{仇討|あだう}ちが{法的|ほうてき}に{認|みと}められていた{時期|じき}がある。
examples.english: There was a period in the Edo era when vendetta was legally recognized.

notes:
USAGE:
{仇討|あだう}ち is closely associated with samurai culture and historical dramas. In modern usage, it can also be used figuratively for getting back at someone or settling a score, especially in sports ({仇討|あだう}ち{戦|せん}, a revenge match).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仇討|あだう}ちを{果|は}たす: to accomplish one's revenge
- {仇討|あだう}ち{戦|せん}: revenge match
- {仇討|あだう}ちの{物語|ものがたり}: a story of vengeance

CULTURAL NOTE:
The most famous {仇討|あだう}ち in Japanese history is the story of the {四十七|しじゅうしち}{士|し} ({赤穂浪士|あこうろうし}), depicted in {忠臣蔵|ちゅうしんぐら}.
